summary.headline: Q4 FY26 presales hit INR 4,288 crores (+69% QoQ) and FY26 presales reached INR 8,136 crores, while BD remained thin at about INR 1,600 crores for the year.
summary.overview: Presales in Q4 FY26 were INR 4,288 crores, up 69% QoQ, on 3 million sq ft of area sold (+75% QoQ), driven by late-March launches in NCR, MMR, Bengaluru and Pune. FY26 presales were INR 8,136 crores, collections INR 3,341 crores and area sold 5.5 million sq ft. Q4 collections of about INR 994 crores were lower YoY and QoQ because March bookings collect in Q1 FY27. Management declined to give FY27 sales guidance and said BD timing is lumpy; it has about INR 60,000 crores of projects under pursuit, of which MMR is about INR 35,000 crores.

financial_highlights.change: Lower YoY and QoQ, per management due to March launches collecting in Q1 FY27
Customer collections grew more than 23% YoY, per management

financial_highlights.value: About INR 38-39 crores (Labour Code impact plus JV provision in textile business)

segments.name: NCR (Birla Arika Phase 2)
segments.commentary: 97% of launch inventory sold in the last quarter, contributing INR 1,600 crores. Six of seven Arika towers are sold; the last tower is being held for a later, higher-priced launch.

segments.name: MMR (Birla Taranya, Niyaara)
segments.commentary: Birla Taranya contributed INR 952 crores of sales, with about INR 960 crores booked in the last days of Q4. Niyaara Tower B has sold about 119 of 148 units; Tower C launch is pending approvals.

segments.name: Bengaluru (Birla Trimaya Phase 4)
segments.commentary: Trimaya Phase 4 contributed INR 649 crores. Last Trimaya phase (about INR 150 crores of inventory) is deferred to maximise pricing; Bengaluru BD is the focus for FY27.

segments.name: Pune (Birla Punya Phase 2)
segments.commentary: Birla Punya Phase 2 added INR 250 crores to Q4 sales. Next Pune launches are Punya (new phase, Q3) and Evam at Manjiri (Q4).

segments.name: Redevelopment
segments.commentary: Maiden redevelopment project in Khar with GDV potential of INR 1,700 crores; development agreement signed and demolition started, with launch targeted in Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 presales guidance. Management cited about INR 9,000 crores of new launches and about INR 7,000 crores of sustenance sales in the current year, but declined to commit.
Construction spend for FY27 is about INR 1,200 crores (FY26: INR 924 crores), per CFO, versus INR 3,131 crores of total project development outflow in FY26 that includes land and overheads.

Launch timing: Niyaara Tower C (Q2/early Q3 FY27, pending RERA at end of Q2), Birla Taranya Phase 2 (Q3), Birla Navya last phase (Q3), Birla Punya new phase (Q3), Khar redevelopment (Q4), Birla Evam Manjiri Pune (Q4). Mathura Road Delhi approvals now expected early FY28.
ITC transaction: CCI approval received; state-level approvals pending; completion expected in the current quarter.
The INR 15,000 crore launch target for FY28 may slip to FY29, per management.
Hurdle IRRs are at least 16% for outright acquisitions and 18-19% for JDA deals.
Customer collections target of 65-70% by completion of structure; collections expected to grow healthily in FY27.
capex_capacity: Construction spend for FY27 is about INR 1,200 crores against INR 924 crores in FY26, per CFO.
Land bank of about INR 70,000-72,000 crores GDV, of which about INR 31,700 crores has been launched; about 70-75% of launched GDV sold (per management, slide 20 of investor presentation).

BD pipeline of about INR 60,000 crores under pursuit, of which MMR about INR 35,000 crores; includes Noida, Gurgaon JDA, Mumbai JDA, 4-5 redevelopment projects, Pune outright, and Bengaluru JDA and outright.

Commercial plans: about 5 lakh sq ft at Birla Taranya (Thane) and one Worli tower of about 1-1.3 million sq ft, with construction targeted to start in FY27; cost not yet estimated. Centurion Phase 2 and Century Bhavan redevelopment also under design.
Talegaon: about 45 acres of agricultural land, not yet converted or under PMRDA; senior living under consideration. Kalyan: no developable land left.
demand_pricing: Industry: MMR pricing up 7.4%, Bengaluru 13.9%, NCR 8.5%, Pune 6% YoY; premium and luxury outperforming while affordable and mid-income softened.

Payment plans were extended in Q4 due to liquidity pressure from Middle East geopolitical developments; management says bulk of offers are construction-linked, targeting 65% collection by structure completion.
Construction material costs up due to oil prices and supply-chain disruption; availability not an issue but transport delays are slight. Contingencies included in business plans.
Bengaluru prices rose with each launch; management is holding last Trimaya phase to maximise pricing.
Management says launches have achieved 97-100% sell-through; no slowdown seen in its own projects yet.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for FY27 sustenance and new-launch sales from the INR 7,300 crore remaining inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects about INR 9,000 crores of new launches and about INR 7,000 crores of sustenance sales this year, but gave no formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the last Trimaya phase not launching this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is holding the phase (about INR 150 crores left) to maximise prices and manage cost escalation, as prices have risen with each launch.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BD pipeline and why has BD been slow?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 60,000 crores under pursuit (MMR about INR 35,000 crores). Management cited IRR hurdles of at least 16% outright and 18-19% for JDA, plus strict due diligence; it expects several deals to be announced together.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY28 launch target of about INR 15,000 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target may slip to FY29 because of BD timing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 presales came through payment plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Bulk of offers are construction-linked; payment-linked plans were extended in Q4 due to liquidity pressure from geopolitical events, with 60-65% still targeted by structure completion.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 collection lower YoY and QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said collections from March bookings will come in Q1 FY27; collection efficiency is 97-98% and April collections were strong.

risks_watch: No formal FY27 sales guidance; management said BD and launch timing are highly uncertain (environmental and NGT approvals).
Niyaara Tower C approvals and RERA timing (Q2/Q3 FY27) and Mathura Road approvals (early FY28) could slip.
BD conversion: about INR 60,000 crores pipeline but only about INR 1,600 crores of BD in FY26; the INR 10,000 crore deal under discussion is still open.
Rising construction costs from oil prices and supply-chain disruption, with a risk of impact if the situation deteriorates.
Payment-plan extensions and geopolitical liquidity stress could signal softer velocity in the market.
ITC transaction completion (state approvals pending) and the quantum of cash proceeds.
summary.management_tone: Confident on sales execution and brand, but cautious and evasive on FY27 guidance, BD timing and launch dates, repeatedly citing approval uncertainty. Management also flagged payment-plan extensions and cost pressures without quantifying them.
key_quotes: We achieved presales of INR 4,288 crores, reflecting a robust 69% Q-o-Q increase.
So any guidance that I give will be -- could be misplaced because of the very sheer uncertainty of when these launches can take place, largely dependent on the approval schedule.
It's not lack of resources or lack of taking calculated risk. It is just the timing and all of these things should come together.
